entities.summary: A major aggadic midrash on the Book of Genesis, compiled in the Land of Israel c. 400–450 CE. Genesis Rabbah provides verse-by-verse commentary on Genesis through homiletical interpretation, parables, and theological reflections by Palestinian Amoraim. It explores creation, patriarchal narratives, divine justice, the nature of good and evil, and Israel's relationship with God. As one of the earliest and most influential midrash collections, it established interpretive frameworks that shaped all subsequent Jewish biblical exegesis and profoundly influenced Christian typological reading of the Old Testament.
